title: Maximize Value of Function in K-Step Passing Game
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array `receiver` of length `n` (`0 <= receiver[i] < n`) and a positive 64-bit integer `k`. Starting with any player `x` (`0 <= x < n`), the ball is passed exactly `k` times: in each pass, the current holder `cur` passes the ball to `receiver[cur]`. The score `f(x)` is the sum of the IDs of all `k + 1` players who hold the ball (including `x` and counting repeated visits). Return the maximum possible value of `f(x)` over all starting players `0 <= x < n`.
hints: Model the `k`-step functional transition as binary lifting (exponentiation by squaring on the function `cur -> receiver[cur]`): track `up[i]` (node reached in `2^b` steps) and `w[i]` (sum of visited receiver IDs along those `2^b` steps).

Maintain `pos[i]` and `score[i]` initialized to `i` for each starting player; iterate over the binary bits of `k`, applying `(up, w)` whenever bit `b` of `k` is `1` and squaring `up` and `w` in O(n) space.

examples.explanation: Starting from player 2 yields sequence 2 -> 1 -> 0 -> 2 -> 1 with sum 2 + 1 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 6.
Starting from player 4 yields sequence 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 with sum 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
Player 0 passes to itself 10^10 times, giving sum 0.
